transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose what made me come in is I had a bit of an outburst. I got upset with one of the younger volunteers over something silly—a tablecloth being crooked—and I spoke more sharply than I should have. I’m not usually like that, and it bothered me afterward.
Do you often find yourself paying attention to small details like that tablecloth being crooked in your daily life?

Not especially, no… I mean, I like things to look tidy, I suppose, but I don’t usually get hung up on little things like that. It just seemed to bother me more than it should have that day. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you consider yourself a perfectionist in other areas of your life?

I wouldn’t really say so, no. I mean, I’ve always tried to do things properly, but not in a way where everything has to be perfect. At least, I don’t think so. If anything, I’d hope I’m fairly easygoing most of the time… does that sound right?
Have you ever found yourself repeatedly thinking about something that you felt you needed to do perfectly, even when it didn't seem that important to others?

No, I don’t think so… not repeatedly like that. I might want to do a decent job, of course, but I can’t say I’ve had something stuck in my mind because it had to be perfect. At least, nothing I’ve really noticed. Is that helpful?
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to act on?

No… I don’t think so. Not urges, anyway. I mean, I suppose everyone has thoughts that come and go, but I haven’t felt like I had to do something over and over or act on it like that. I hope that’s answering what you mean.
Have you ever been told that you can come across as stubborn or overly insistent on doing things your own way?

Not that I can recall, no. I mean, I suppose I can have my preferences like anyone, especially after doing things a certain way for many years, but I don’t think people have called me stubborn or anything like that. At least not seriously. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you often find it difficult to change your plans or adapt to new situations?

No, not especially. I mean, I like knowing what I’m doing for the day, but if something changes, I can usually go along with it. I don’t think I get unusually upset or stuck on a plan. At least, I haven’t noticed that about myself. Does that answer it?
Do you tend to have very strong opinions about how things should be done?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have my opinions like anyone does, especially about little routines at home, but I wouldn’t say they’re very strong or that I need people to do things my way. If anything, I try not to make a fuss. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you ever felt like you had habits or behaviors that you couldn't stop doing, even if you wanted to?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have little habits like anyone—checking I’ve got my keys, keeping things in a certain place—but nothing I feel I can’t stop doing. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that what you mean?
Have you experienced any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to dismiss?

Yes… I suppose there are a few thoughts, or pictures really, that come back. I don’t want to make too much of it, but out of nowhere I’ll hear that man’s rough voice in my head, or I’ll see the donation envelope hitting the ground. It can happen when I’m just sitting at my kitchen table, not doing anything in particular. I try to push it aside, and sometimes I can, but it does sort of stick there. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these thoughts or pictures that come back to you feel like they're something you'd rather not think about, or are they more like reflections or memories that you're willingly considering?

No, I wouldn’t say I’m choosing to think about them. They just sort of pop in… like I’ll be sitting at the kitchen table and suddenly I hear that man’s rough voice again, or I see the donation envelope hit the ground. I’d rather not have it come up, honestly, though I try not to make too much of it. Is that what you mean by intrusive?
Do these thoughts or pictures that come back to you cause you a lot of upset or anxiety when they happen?

It does upset me some, yes. I wouldn’t say I fall apart or anything like that, but when it comes out of nowhere—hearing that man’s rough voice again, or seeing that donation envelope hit the ground—it gives me a jolt. I don’t like it. I try to tell myself it’s just a memory and move on, but it can leave me feeling uneasy for a bit. Is that… is that the sort of upset you mean?
When these intrusive thoughts or pictures come into your mind, do you feel like you need to do something to make them go away or to prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of having to do some particular thing, or feeling like something bad will happen if I don’t. I might take a breath, or try to think about something else, but that’s just to settle myself a bit. I haven’t noticed any, um, ritual or anything like that. Is that what you were asking?
Did something particularly stressful or traumatic happen around the time you started experiencing these intrusive thoughts or pictures?

Yes… yes, I suppose it did start after the robbery outside the bank. It’s only been about a week, so I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but that’s when those pictures and thoughts started coming up.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the robbery outside the bank?

A little, yes… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m hiding away or anything. But I have been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass the bank. And I haven’t gone into the festival storage room since then, because it just… brings the whole thing too close, if that makes sense. I know that probably sounds silly, but that’s what I’ve been doing.
How long have you been avoiding the bank and the festival storage room?
About a week, I think… pretty much since the robbery happened outside the bank. I know that’s not very long, but that’s when I started going out of my way to avoid those places.
Have you been avoiding anything else besides the bank and the festival storage room?

No, I don’t think so… not really. It’s mostly just those two things—the bank, so I take the longer way, and the festival storage room, because going in there makes it feel too close again. I hope that makes sense.
How much distress do you feel when you think about going to the bank or the festival storage room?

It’s… not overwhelming, I don’t think. I can manage it. But when I picture going past the bank, I get pretty uneasy, enough that I just take the long way around instead. And the festival storage room is similar — going in there makes everything feel too close again, so I’ve just stayed out of it. I know maybe that sounds like I’m making more of it than I should, but it does bother me.
